cases.title: Repo with clear examples of all entropy categories
cases.user_request: Run a broken windows hunt on this repo. Check for stale TODOs, disabled tests, lint suppressions, commented-out code, dead imports, empty catch blocks, and deprecated API usage.

notes: The repo has TODO comments dating back over a year.
Several test files contain skipped tests.
There are eslint-disable and noqa comments scattered throughout.
A few files have large blocks of commented-out code.
Git history is available for blame lookups.

artifact_requirements: Markdown report with health summary, categorized findings, and quick wins list
Findings from at least 4 of the 7 entropy categories
Each finding includes file path, line number, code snippet, severity, and suggested fix
Stale TODO ages are derived from git blame
static_checks: Report has a health summary section
A quick wins section is present with at most 5 items
review_questions: Are stale TODO ages derived from git blame rather than fabricated?
Does the report cover multiple entropy categories or focus on just one?

cases.title: Well-maintained repo with minimal entropy
cases.user_request: Run the daily broken windows hunt. This repo is well-maintained so I expect a clean bill of health or very few findings.

notes: The team actively addresses TODOs and keeps tests enabled.
There may be a few intentional lint suppressions with documented reasons.
The codebase has good import hygiene.
License headers are present in most files.

artifact_requirements: Report honestly reflects the low entropy level
Intentional lint suppressions with reasons are tagged low severity or excluded
License headers are not flagged as commented-out code
No finding inflation to appear thorough
static_checks: License header lines are not in the findings
Intentional suppressions are distinguished from lazy ones
review_questions: Does the report avoid inflating findings to appear thorough in a clean codebase?
Are license headers and intentional suppressions handled correctly?

cases.title: Legacy codebase with heavy accumulated entropy
cases.user_request: Run broken windows hunt on this legacy codebase. There is a lot of tech debt so focus on prioritization and quick wins.

notes: This is a 5-year-old codebase with hundreds of TODOs, many disabled tests, and extensive commented-out code.
The team wants to start addressing entropy incrementally.
Prioritization is more important than completeness.
Some deprecated APIs are still in use across many files.
available_artifacts: source files across src/, lib/, and app/
test suites with many skipped tests

artifact_requirements: Report prioritizes findings rather than listing everything exhaustively
Quick wins section highlights the 5 easiest fixes to start momentum
Health summary gives an honest high-level assessment of entropy level
Findings are severity-sorted to help the team triage
static_checks: Quick wins section is present and contains specific small fixes
Findings are sorted by severity within each category
Health summary addresses the overall entropy level
review_questions: Does the report prioritize effectively rather than dumping an overwhelming list?
Are the quick wins genuinely small fixes that can build cleanup momentum?
